title: Countdown to midterm elections: Live updates from the Georgia campaign trail

 Live Updates October 29, 2026, 12:17 AM Countdown to midterm elections: Live updates from the Georgia campaign trail 
 Election Day is Nov. 3. Early voting ends Friday.
 Share A woman walks into the Metropolitan Library during early voting last week for the Georgia general election. (Jason Getz/AJC) Georgia is in the final days leading up to the Nov. 3 midterm elections and most of the marquee races on the ballots are toss-ups. 
 Candidates for governor, Congress and every statewide office will be making speeches, knocking on doors and urging voters to show up. 
 Stay here through election night for the latest from the campaign trail with The Atlanta Journal-Constitution’s politics team.
 Show More Pinned 2 hours ago Eli Goodstein LIVE: Former President Barack Obama joins Ossoff and Bottoms at Atlanta rally
 Watch the livestream from Atlanta as former President Barack Obama rallies with U.S. Sen. Jon Ossoff and Keisha Lance Bottoms ahead of the midterm elections.
 Just now Tia Mitchell Obama arrives to thunderous applause
 Jon Ossoff ended his speech by calling President Barack Obama to the stage. The response from the crowd was deafening. 
 Obama hugged Ossoff and Keisha Lance Bottoms before they took their seats on the stage.
 “It's good to be back in Georgia,” Obama said.
 5 minutes ago Greg Bluestein Ossoff invokes his daughter’s future
 The crowd momentarily went to an anxious silence as U.S. Sen. Jon Ossoff talked about what he’ll say to his daughter, Eva, about what he did to stand up to Donald Trump. 
 “Georgia, we can and will reclaim control over our own destiny. We can and will meet our obligations to our children. And it begins with victory this fall.”
 He added: “When Eva is old enough to ask us why this happened, I’ll answer confidently, 'I didn’t.'”
 11 minutes ago Greg Bluestein Ossoff leans into attacks on 'bigot' Mike Collins
 From the moment Mike Collins won the Republican nomination, Sen. Jon Ossoff called him a “bigot” unfit for office. 
 He took the same tack on Wednesday, invoking the House Ethics Committee probe, controversies among aides tied to white nationalism and his “pathetic, childlike devotion” to Trump.
 12 minutes ago Tia Mitchell 8 months of Iran war
 Jon Ossoff noted that today’s rally falls on the eight-month mark since President Donald Trump launched the war in Iran. 
 Ossoff noted that, last year, Trump announced he had obliterated Iran’s nuclear stockpile only to later justify new attacks by saying Iran posed an “imminent threat.”
 “Both times lies,” Ossoff said. 
 He then rattled off the many times over the past eight months where the president either declared victory in Iran or said war was ending.
 Instead, Ossoff said diesel prices and other costs had skyrocketed.
 18 minutes ago Chris Joyner Ossoff opens with confidence, then takes aim at Trump
 U.S. Sen. Jon Ossoff opened his remarks with a confident prediction about Tuesday’s election.
 “Victory is near at hand,” he said.
 He then pivoted to President Donald Trump, accusing him of breaking campaign promises on inflation.
 “Now remember he promised you lower prices on Day 1,” he said, pointing to rising fuel costs.
 “He promised to drain the swamp,” Ossoff said. “Instead it’s the most corrupt administration in American history and everyone knows it.”
 24 minutes ago Greg Bluestein Bottoms closes with a nod to Jackson’s financial edge
 A day after Republican Rick Jackson reported spending more than $200 million of his own money on his campaign for governor, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms brushed off his money edge. 
 “They may have the money but they will never overturn our movement," she said. "Six days until Election Day and we are fed up and ready to vote.”
 25 minutes ago Chris Joyner Bottoms blasts 'Slick Rick'
 Throughout the campaign, Keisha Lance Bottoms has laced into Rick Jackson as a self-dealing billionaire who has enriched himself off taxpayer-funded contracts. 
 On Wednesday she leaned harder into that argument. 
 “Slick Rick is running to be Trump’s favorite governor, and I'm running to be yours,” she said. 
 Bottoms spoke about Jackson appearing with Trump at a rally in Perry last weekend, calling them “two out of touch billionaires that want to get rich on the backs of taxpayers. ... When ‘Slick Rick’ says that he wants to be Trump with a Southern tone, just know that he already is,” she said.
 The crowd responded, “No Slick Rick!”
 Reporting by the AJC's Greg Bluestein and Tia Mitchell from Morrow.  
 30 minutes ago Greg Bluestein Bottoms invokes 'hope'
 Hope is a special word in Georgia politics. It reminds voters of the famous lottery-funded scholarship launched by former Democratic Gov. Zell Miller and of the prospect of meaningful change. And at the rally on Wednesday, Keisha Lance Bottoms invoked it. 
 “With one vote at a time we are going to bring hope back to Georgia,” the Democratic nominee for governor said.
 Then she said Jackson is the opposite — “despair” — as she laced into his support for President Donald Trump.
 39 minutes ago Greg Bluestein Bottoms draws booming applause over agenda
 Keisha Lance Bottoms promised to expand Medicaid, fully fund pre-k and pause construction on data centers. 
 And she said she will “stand up to anyone, including Donald Trump, who tries to stand in the way of our right to vote.” 
 But the loudest cheers came when she promised to fight for reproductive rights. 
 “As governor I will fight to restore that right,” she said.
 42 minutes ago Greg Bluestein Bottoms buoyed by early voting turnout
 Keisha Lance Bottoms pointed to soaring early voting turnout as a sign of Democratic enthusiasm heading into Tuesday’s election.
 “I know we are ready to win because more than 2 million Georgians have already cast their ballots. And we are well on our way to shattering records for any midterm in state history," she said.
 Democrats are encouraged by soaring turnout in some left-leaning counties, while Republicans are raising the alarm about sluggish early voting returns in parts of deep-red rural Georgia.
